lastReleaseMessage: the version pill and the changelog catch up with what is deployed

milestone.label: v0.16 - Supabase auth + Stripe subscriptions + live TICA data pipeline

items: RE-COUNTED 2026-09-02 against the same eight gates and HELD at 84, because no gate moved. The counting rule is written down here so the next audit can re-derive the number in a minute instead of asking the question a fourth time: each of the eight version-one gates in the Version-one scope section of PROJECT_SPEC.md is worth 12.5 points, a gate scores full when it is shipped, and a gate whose code is finished but whose last step is a ruling or a reading nobody has taken yet scores partial. Six gates are shipped, so the floor is 75. The two open gates, the free-tier measurement and the billing enforcement flag, are both code-complete with one non-code step left each, so the defensible band runs from 75 at no credit to 87.5 at half credit, and 84 sits inside it. What happened since the 2026-08-26 anchor is repair work on gates that were already counted, not a gate closing: v0.18.0 fixed a Stripe webhook that had answered 500 on every delivery since the event log landed, migration 0012 granted back the execute permission migration 0009 revoked, and v0.18.1 made the audit trail say so when its durable write fails. The billing gate is in better shape than it was on the anchor date and still is not enforcing, so the number stays where it is. Moving it needs a gate to close.

RE-COUNTED 2026-08-26 against an approved scope, which is why the number finally moved. It sat at 76 through three reviews because the completion question could not be answered while the freeze-versus-phase-two decision was open: a percentage needs a denominator, and there was not one. Kane ruled keep building, under a no-cost-increase constraint, and the scope is now eight gates written into the Version-one scope section of PROJECT_SPEC.md. Six of the eight are shipped. Three of them closed today in v0.17.36: data stewardship (export, erasure, retention policy, public retention page), durability (the community judge ratings now have a daily Postgres snapshot, migration 0010, and were the last dataset with no second copy), and the code half of running inside the free tier. Four surfaces moved out of the count entirely rather than being finished, and that is a real part of the change: the ten-table relational schema in 0001_init.sql is parked in the file itself, along with ownership certificate verification, the invite flow, and merged co-ownership. They were counting against completion while nobody intended to build them.
Billing gate: the Stripe subscription path is code-complete and one environment flag (SUBSCRIPTION_GATE_ENFORCE) from enforcing. Turning it on or deciding not to is the open gate.

Free-tier measurement: the write budget is now understood and the code is inside it, but nobody has read the actual key-value write counts off the Cloudflare dashboard. That reading needs an account token this session was not permitted to use, so the arithmetic in PROJECT_SPEC.md is unverified against real traffic.
Judge-panel coverage keeps converging by cron. Ongoing by design, not a gate that closes.

Security: view-as and shared-cats still read the key-value store rather than security-definer remote calls, so the two cross-account paths lack the database-enforced boundary that own-data reads have. Carried, not scoped as a version-one gate.

Read the Postgres copy alongside the key-value copy before short-circuiting, and skip the write only when both agree.

Skip the write when the tally read returns nothing, rather than defaulting it to zero.
Exempt the newest complete snapshot from the prune, keeping it alongside the thirty most recent rows.
Extend the tell-vocabulary ratchet to the courtesy-offer phrase, first-person collective pronouns and named assistant tools, since three of the four rules CLAUDE.md states have no automated check.
Delete one of tokenOf or bearer and point every call site at the survivor, so a change to token parsing cannot land in only one of the two.

Name Discord and Resend in privacy.html, or add a feedback row to its storage table, since feedback carries an optional email and free text to two third parties the page does not mention.
Wrap the email interpolation in pgStateWrite two console.error calls with maskEmail, matching every comparable log line in the same file.
Add a rate-limit bucket to the view-as branch of the state read, matching every other gated route.
Treat a missing judge tally as no recorded vote in handleJudgeRating, so an admin reset that deletes j: but leaves jv: markers cannot lock prior voters out of re-casting.
Hash or strip the address segment of each vote key before it enters the snapshot, or scrub that table on erasure.
Extend the calendar-list refusal guard to the per-show detail write, so a markup change on shows.tica.org cannot silently replace a good judge panel with an empty one.

Point the setup instructions and example file in discord-notify.ps1 at the centralized secrets folder the script actually reads, and remove the dead local copies.
Call the status writer with a skipped outcome before both early exits, or drop the not-configured claim from the comment.
Check the exit code of write-dashboard-status.ps1 in release.ps1 and surface a failed status write, because the failure is currently swallowed at every layer.
Extend the integrity guard in push-to-github.ps1 to assert those four files end cleanly or meet a size floor against the previous committed copy.
Add extraction markers and a fixture test for titleProgress mirroring merge-states.test.js, covering the first ladder step, the last, and a points value exactly on a threshold.
Call recordCronError inside the audit-log catch so a broken privileged-action log surfaces on the health route.
Add a super-admin route, gated the way the parity route already is, that returns the newest audit entries.
Run the 63 breed line-art files through an optimizer at one or two decimal precision and commit the reduced versions, because single icons run 100 to 300 kilobytes for a 64 to 120 pixel render.
Re-run hydrate when the tab becomes visible again, the way the existing give-up retry already does for pushes.
Give the null-byte strip and the build stamp a real failure path, or rewrite the gate description in CLAUDE.md, because two of the seven documented pre-flight gates have no failure condition at all.
Route searchStandings through tmText so an upstream 403 or 500 raises rather than parsing to zero matches, which currently reads as a cat that does not exist.

Collect the settled results of the five erasure key-value deletions and report any failure in the response and the audit entry, instead of telling the person their data is gone over a swallowed error.
Log the non-ok status and the thrown reason in verifyUser, so an identity-provider outage is distinguishable from an invalid token instead of answering 401 everywhere in silence.
Route the 404 branch through recordCronError so a Worker running ahead of migration 0013 shows on the health route as a billing fault.

Record in the Cost constraint table that the season sweep grows by one season a year against a fixed subrequest cap, and decide now whether SEASON_FLOOR becomes a rolling window.

Cap the sh: and shby: grant arrays or split sharing into one key per grant, since they are the one multi-item namespace read and rewritten in full with no bound.
Export parseShowDetail through __testables and add fixture tests for the judge panel and counts, mirroring calendar-floor.test.js, since the detail parser has no coverage at all.

Stamp merge keys from a server-supplied clock or correct for the client offset, because per-key last-writer-wins currently lets a device with a wrong clock win every conflict.
Send a stable idempotency key on the Stripe customer create, so an abort after Stripe has already created the customer cannot mint a second one and split a billing history.

Set actedOn from whether billingSync actually ran, so a matched type that wrote nothing is stamped ignored.

closedLog.evidence: an event type this app does not act on is stamped ignored rather than applied, through a new stripe_event_ignore function in migration 0013, so an ignored delivery stops raising the per-customer staleness watermark. Commit 490bb15, with a new webhook test and the migration probe updated to six guarded functions. Commit da90f1b then made the stamp survive a worker deployed ahead of its migration: a

handleUserDelete erases the durable copy first and aborts with 502 postgres_unavailable before touching any key-value store when that erasure is not confirmed, so an outage can no longer destroy the fast copy, the sharing grants and the vote markers while the durable account row survives. Commit 490bb15, with two new tests. Verified 2026-09-04 by running npm test in X:/YesAndRing: 144 of 144 pass.

handleStatePost reads the last written blob and skips both writes when the incoming state and name are unchanged under a stable serialization, reporting unchanged, and PROJECT_SPEC.md gains the write-volume row in the cost table. Commits 490bb15 and dc21e28, with a new four-case test covering the no-op skip, a key-order-only change, a real edit and the first save. Verified 2026-09-04 by running np
